nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
(يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ): «النّاس» is nominative (marfūʿ) as a naʿt (adjective) of «أيّ». Al-Māzinī allowed the accusative on the basis of the position, as you say: «يا زيدُ الكريمَ أقبل». Abū Isḥāq said: This is an error on al-Māzinī's part, because with «زيد» it is permissible to pause and stop at it alone, whereas «يا أيّها» alone is not permissible, and «النّاس» are the ones intended [by the address].
The meaning is: «يا ناسُ اتّقوا ربّكم» (O people, fear your Lord). (إِنَّ زَلْزَلَةَ السَّاعَةِ): that is, its terrors, the quaking of the earth, and the dazzling signs.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t:
(يَوْمَ تَرَوْنَها تَذْهَلُ كُلُّ مُرْضِعَةٍ)
Abū Isḥāq said: «تذهل» means: becomes bewildered and abandons. «مرضعة» runs on the verb, because after it comes (أَرْضَعَتْ).
The Kufans say: whatever is specific to the feminine does not take the hāʾ [of the feminine], such as «حائض» (menstruating) and «طالق» (divorced) and the like. ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said:
The proof that this view is mistaken is the presence of the hāʾ in its place [here]. (وَتَرَى النَّاسَ سُكارى وَما هُمْ بِسُكارى)
that is, it is from the severity of the terror and the trembling of the heart. Abū Hurayra read (وَتَرَى النَّاسَ سُكارى) «[Translator's note: the variant reading itself has evidently been lost in the printed text; it is given here in the same form as the standard reading.]»
— the two are then two objects (mafʿūlān). Sībawayh said: one says «سُكارى» and «سَكارى». He said: and some people say «سَكْرى», likening it to «مَرْضى» (sick ones), because it is an affliction that enters upon the intellect, like illness. Abū Jaʿfar said:
Sībawayh's saying "and some people say «سكرى»" indicates that the other usage is better known than this one.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: (وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يُجادِلُ فِي اللَّهِ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ وَيَتَّبِعُ كُلَّ شَيْطانٍ مَرِيدٍ) (3): «مَنْ» is in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and «يجادل» follows the wording; outside the Qurʾān «يجادلون» would be permissible, following the meaning. (وَيَتَّبِعُ كُلَّ شَيْطانٍ مَرِيدٍ): one says «مريد» and «مارد» of one who goes to excess in evil and is strong in it; and «صخرة مرداء» means a smooth rock, and from it is said «أمرد» (beardless youth).

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: (كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِ أَنَّهُ مَنْ تَوَلَّاهُ): «أنّ» is in the position of nominative; (فَأَنَّهُ يُضِلُّهُ) is conjoined to it. The view of Sībawayh is that the second «أنّ» is repeated for tawkīd (emphasis), and that the meaning is: «كتب عليه أنّه من تولّاه يضلّه». Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: the implied form is «كتب عليه أنّه من تولّاه فالواجبُ أن يضلّه», with the hamza vowelled with fatḥa; and whoever claims that «أنّ» is in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ has erred, because Sībawayh disallowed beginning [a sentence] with the «أنّ» that has fatḥa. Sībawayh allowed (كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِ أَنَّهُ مَنْ تَوَلَّاهُ فَإِنَّهُ يُضِلُّهُ) with kasra on the hamza, because the fāʾ is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), so what follows it should be a mubtadaʾ, and the beginning [of a sentence] with «إنّ» is with kasra. (وَيَهْدِيهِ إِلى عَذابِ السَّعِيرِ) is figurative (majāz): since he commands him to what leads him to the Fire, that takes the place of guiding him to it.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t:
(يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ فِي رَيْبٍ مِنَ الْبَعْثِ): the grammarians relate «من البَعَث» «[Translator's note: the printed text shows the word without the vowelling that distinguishes the variant; the discussion that follows shows it is «البَعَث» with fatḥa on the ʿayn.]». The Kufans allowed, in every word whose second letter is one of the guttural letters, that it be given sukūn or fatḥa, such as «نَعْل» and «نَعَل», «بُخْل» and «بَخَل». Abū Isḥāq said: This is a mistake; in this one returns only to the [attested] language, so one says «لفلانٍ عليَّ وَعْد» (so-and-so has a promise from me) and one does not say «وَعَد»; there is no difference in this between the guttural letters and others; this is only like «قَدْر» and «قَدَر». Abū ʿUbayd said: «العلقة» is blood when its redness becomes intense. Al-Kisāʾī said: (مُخَلَّقَةً) in the accusative is permissible, and (وَغَيْرَ مُخَلَّقَةٍ), on the verb and on qaṭʿ (detachment). (لِنُبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ), that is, so that We make clear to you Our power to form whatever We will. Abū Ḥātim related from Abū Zayd from al-Mufaḍḍal from ʿĀṣim (لِنُبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ وَنُقِرَّ فِي الْأَرْحامِ ما نَشاءُ) with the accusative. (إِلى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى ثُمَّ نُخْرِجُكُمْ طِفْلًا).
Abū Ḥātim said: the accusative is by conjunction. Abū Isḥāq said: (وَنُقِرُّ) is nominative and nothing else, because the meaning is not "We did that in order to settle in the wombs what We will", since Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not create humankind in order to settle in the wombs what He wills; He created them only to guide them to right conduct and righteousness. He said: «طفل» means «أطفال» (infants). He said: the plural wording [«نخرجكم»] indicates that. He said: and it contains the meaning "and He brings out each one of you as an infant".
Whoever reads (وَمِنْكُمْ مَنْ يَتَوَفَّى) «[Translator's note: the printed text has the standard vowelling «يُتَوَفَّى»; the explanation that follows indicates the active reading «يَتَوَفَّى».]», its meaning for him is "he completes his term in full". (وَمِنْكُمْ مَنْ يُرَدُّ إِلى أَرْذَلِ الْعُمُرِ), that is, to old age, because he does not hope for strength or long life, so he is in the most abject [stage] of life. (لِكَيْلا يَعْلَمَ مِنْ بَعْدِ عِلْمٍ شَيْئاً): the view of al-Farrāʾ is: so that he understands nothing after his first understanding. (مِنْ كُلِّ زَوْجٍ بَهِيجٍ): al-Kisāʾī said: one says «بَهُجَ بهجةً وبهاجةً» (to be beautiful, delightful).

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: The position of «ذلك» is nominative, with the meaning «الأمرُ ذلك» (the matter is that). Abū Isḥāq said: it may be in the position of accusative, with the meaning «فَعَلَ اللهُ ذلك بأنّه الحقّ» «[Translator's note: the printed text reads «لأنه الحق»; the verse has (بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْحَقُّ).]» — that is, "Allah did that because He is the Truth".

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: (وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يُجادِلُ فِي اللَّهِ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ): [«مَن»] is in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: (ثانِيَ عِطْفِهِ) is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). It is interpreted in two senses. One of them: it is related from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: it is al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, who twisted his neck out of exultation and self-importance. The other sense, which is the view of al-Farrāʾ: the implied form is «ومن الناس من يجادل في الله بغير علم ثانيَ عطفه», that is, turning away from the Reminder.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: (ذلِكَ بِما قَدَّمَتْ يَداكَ): Abū Isḥāq said: «ذلك» is in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is (بِما قَدَّمَتْ يَداكَ). (وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ) is in the position of genitive (khafḍ), conjoined to the first; it may also be in the position of nominative with the meaning «والأمرُ أنّ الله ليس بظلّامٍ للعبيد» (and the matter is that Allah is not unjust to His servants). He said: the kasra is also permissible: «وإنّ الله».

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: (وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَعْبُدُ اللَّهَ عَلى حَرْفٍ): [«مَن»] is in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). The complete [stop] is at (انْقَلَبَ عَلى وَجْهِهِ) according to the reading of those who read (خَسِرَ). Mujāhid and Ḥumayd read «خاسرَ الدنيا والآخرة» in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). He lost this world through Allah, Mighty and Majestic, censuring him and commanding that he be cursed, and that he have no share in booty nor in praise; and he lost the Hereafter in that he has no reward in it.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: (ذلِكَ هُوَ الضَّلالُ الْبَعِيدُ): al-Farrāʾ said: that is, the long one.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: (يَدْعُوا لَمَنْ ضَرُّهُ أَقْرَبُ مِنْ نَفْعِهِ): we have mentioned several views on it. Among them is the view of al-Kisāʾī that the lām is out of its place, and that the implied form is «يدعو مَن لَضرُّه أقربُ من نفعه». Abū Jaʿfar said: The lām does not have the freedom of movement that would make fronting and postponing it permissible. ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān related to us from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad], who said: there is an ellipsis in the speech, and the meaning is «يدعو لَمَن ضرُّه أقربُ من نفعه إلهاً» (he calls, as a god, upon one whose harm is nearer than his benefit). He said: I think this view has been wrongly attributed to Muḥammad ibn Yazīd, because it makes no sense, since what follows the lām is a mubtadaʾ, so the accusative «إلهاً» is not permissible; and I think the view of Muḥammad ibn Yazīd can only be the view of al-Akhfash Saʿīd, which is to me the best that has been said about the verse, and Allah knows best. He said: «يدعو» means «يقول» (says), and «مَن» is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar (predicate) is omitted; the meaning is: «يقول: لَمَن ضرُّه أقربُ من نفعه إلهُه» (he says: the one whose harm is nearer than his benefit is surely his god). Had the lām been with kasra, the meaning would be "he calls to one whose harm is nearer than his benefit". And Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said: (بِأَنَّ رَبَّكَ أَوْحى لَها) [al-Zalzala: 5], that is, «إليها» (to it). (لَبِئْسَ الْمَوْلى): [«المولى»] is in the position of nominative by «بئس». We have already explained the like of this.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: The grammarians have spoken about the meaning of this verse and about clarifying what is difficult in it. Among the best of what has been said about it is that the meaning is: whoever thinks that Allah, Majestic and Mighty, will not help Muḥammad ﷺ, and that it is possible for him to cut off the help he has been given, "let him stretch a rope (سبب) to the sky", that is, let him seek some device by which he can reach the sky; (ثُمَّ لْيَقْطَعْ), that is, then let him cut off the help, if that is possible for him; (فَلْيَنْظُرْ هَلْ يُذْهِبَنَّ كَيْدُهُ) and his device what enrages him of the help given to the Prophet ﷺ. The point of the speech is that if scheming and contrivance to do such a thing are not possible for him, he will not manage to cut off the help. The people of Kufa read [«ثُمَّ لْيَقْطَعْ»] with the lām given sukūn. This is far-fetched in Arabic, because «ثمّ» is not like the wāw and the fāʾ, since one can pause on it and it stands on its own.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَالَّذِينَ هادُوا): the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ» is (إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَهُمْ). Al-Farrāʾ said: in ordinary speech «إنّ زيداً إنّ أخاه منطلق» is not permissible; he claimed that it was permissible in the verse only because the speech carries the meaning of a conditional (mujāzāh), that is: whoever believes, and whoever becomes a Jew, or a Christian, or a Sabian, then the judgement between them and their reckoning rests with Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Abū Isḥāq rejected this from al-Farrāʾ and considered his statement «إنّ زيداً إنّ أخاه منطلق» [being disallowed] objectionable. He said: because there is no difference between «زيد» and «الذي», and «إنّ» enters upon every mubtadaʾ, so you say «إنّ زيداً هو منطلق», then you bring «إنّ» and say «إنّ زيداً إنّه منطلق».

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: [«والشمس»] «[Translator's note: the word under discussion is not quoted in the printed text; from the context it is (وَالشَّمْسُ).]» is conjoined to «مَن», and likewise (وَالْقَمَرُ وَالنُّجُومُ وَالْجِبالُ وَالشَّجَرُ وَالدَّوَابُّ وَكَثِيرٌ مِنَ النَّاسِ). Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: (وَكَثِيرٌ حَقَّ عَلَيْهِ الْعَذابُ), and this is a difficult point of i'rab. It is asked: why was it not made accusative, so that what the verb governs is conjoined to what a verb governs, like (وَالظَّالِمِينَ أَعَدَّ لَهُمْ عَذاباً أَلِيماً) [al-Insān: 31]? Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ claimed that had it been made accusative it would have been good, but the nominative was chosen because the meaning is "and many refused to prostrate". There is another view on its nominative: it is conjoined to the first and included in the prostration, because prostration here is only submission to Allah's ordering, Majestic and Mighty, in weakness and strength, health and sickness, beauty and ugliness, and everything is included in this. Al-Kisāʾī, al-Akhfash and al-Farrāʾ related (وَمَنْ يُهِنِ اللَّهُ فَما لَهُ مِنْ مُكْرَمٍ) «[Translator's note: the printed text has the standard «مُكْرِمٍ»; the gloss "honouring" indicates the reading «مُكْرَمٍ», a maṣdar.]», that is, "of any honouring".

nahhas-irab:19-19.t:
Ibn Kathīr and Shibl read (هذانِّ خَصْمانِ) with the nūn doubled. There are two views about this: one is that its doubling is a compensation for what was dropped from «هذين»; the other is that it [the nūn] is not dropped in iḍāfa (annexation). Al-Farrāʾ interpreted the two disputants as two parties, the people of two religions; he claimed that one disputant is the Muslims and the other the Jews and Christians, who disputed about the religion of their Lord. He said: He said «اختصموا» (they disputed, plural) because they are a group.
He said: had He said «اختصما» (dual) it would have been permissible. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is the interpretation of someone with no experience of ḥadīth nor of the books of the people of tafsīr, because the ḥadīth about this verse is well known. Sufyān al-Thawrī and others related it from Abū Hāshim from Abū Mijlaz from Qays ibn ʿUbād, who said: I heard Abū Dharr swear an oath that this verse was revealed concerning Ḥamza, ʿAlī and ʿUbayda ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, and ʿUtba and Shayba the two sons of Rabīʿa, and al-Walīd ibn ʿUtba. Likewise Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ related from Mujāhid from Ibn ʿAbbās.

nahhas-irab:20-20.t:
(يُصْهَرُ بِهِ ما فِي بُطُونِهِمْ): [«ما»] is nominative by a verb whose agent is not named (the passive). (وَالْجُلُودُ) is conjoined to «ما». Al-Kisāʾī said: one says «صهرتُه», meaning "I cooked it through". The Kufans say: the meaning of «والجلود» is:
«وجلودُهم» (and their skins).

nahhas-irab:23-23.t:
Abū Isḥāq said: it is also read «ويَحْلَوْن فيها من أساور من ذهب», from your saying «حَلِيَ يَحْلى» when someone comes to have ornaments. He said: (وَلُؤْلُؤاً) in the sense «ويُحَلَّوْن لؤلؤاً» (and they are adorned with pearls). He said: and «لؤلؤٍ» [in the genitive] in the sense:
«ومن لؤلؤ» (and of pearls). He said: and it may be that this is a mixture of the two.

nahhas-irab:24-24.t: (وَهُدُوا إِلَى الطَّيِّبِ مِنَ الْقَوْلِ): there are three views on it: in the language it may be taken generally; it has been said: the good of speech is the fine glad tidings; and it has been said: it is their saying (الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَذْهَبَ عَنَّا الْحَزَنَ) [Fāṭir: 34].

nahhas-irab:25-25.t:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا): [«الذين»] is the noun (ism) of «إنّ», and (كَفَرُوا) is its ṣila (relative clause); (وَيَصُدُّونَ) is conjoined to «الذين كفروا». If it is asked: how is an imperfect conjoined to a past? There are three views on it: one is that it is the conjoining of a clause to a clause; another is that it is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), as you say: «كلّمتُ زيداً وهو جالس» (I spoke to Zayd while he was sitting); and Abū Isḥāq said: it is conjoined according to the meaning, because the meaning is "Those who disbelieve and those who bar from the Sacred Mosque". On the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ» there are three views. The soundest is that it is omitted, the meaning being: «إنّ الذين كفروا ويصدّون عن سبيل الله هلكوا» (those who disbelieve and bar from the way of Allah have perished). It has been said: the meaning is «إنّ الذين كفروا يصدّون عن سبيل الله», and the wāw is inserted (muqḥama). Abū Jaʿfar said: In my copy from Abū Isḥāq, he said: it is permissible that it be — and this is the way of the khabar — (نُذِقْهُ مِنْ عَذابٍ أَلِيمٍ). Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a mistake, and I do not know what the reasoning in it is, because he has made the khabar of «إنّ» jussive; moreover it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the condition, and were it the khabar the condition would remain without an apodosis — especially since the verb of the condition is imperfect, so it must have an apodosis.
(الَّذِي جَعَلْناهُ لِلنَّاسِ سَواءً الْعاكِفُ فِيهِ وَالْبادِ): there are three readings on it. The reading of the generality is with «سواءٌ», «العاكفُ» and «البادي» in the nominative. It is related from Abū al-Aswad al-Duʾalī that he read «سواءً العاكفُ فيه والبادي», with «سواء» accusative and «العاكف» and «البادي» nominative; this reading is also related from al-Aʿmash, with disagreement over [what is reported from] him. The third: (الَّذِي جَعَلْناهُ لِلنَّاسِ سَواءً), accusative with tanwīn,
«العاكفِ فيه» in the genitive. The first reading has three analyses. «الذي جعلناه للناس» completes the speech, then you say «سواءٌ» and make it nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar being «العاكف فيه والبادي». The second analysis: you make «سواء» nominative as the khabar of «العاكف», intending it to come later, that is: «العاكفُ فيه والبادي سواءٌ». The third analysis: the hāʾ in «جعلناه» is the first object, and «سواءٌ العاكفُ فيه والبادي» is in the position of the second object, as you say: «ظننتُ زيداً أبوه خارجٌ» (I thought Zayd's father was going out). From this analysis comes the reading of whoever reads «سواءً» in the accusative, making it the second object, with «العاكف فيه» nominative; except that the preferred option in such a case, according to Sībawayh, is the nominative, because it does not run on the verb [i.e. it is not a participle]. The third reading is on the basis that «سواء» is accusative because it is the second object, and «العاكف» is genitive because it is a naʿt (adjective) of «الناس»; the implied form is:
«الذي جعلناه للناس العاكفِ فيه والبادي سواءً». (وَمَنْ يُرِدْ فِيهِ بِإِلْحادٍ بِظُلْمٍ) is a condition, and its apodosis is (نُذِقْهُ مِنْ عَذابٍ أَلِيمٍ). ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās (وَمَنْ يُرِدْ فِيهِ بِإِلْحادٍ بِظُلْمٍ): he said: [it is] shirk (associating partners with Allah). ʿAṭāʾ said: shirk and killing. We have already mentioned this verse.

nahhas-irab:26-27.t:
(وَإِذْ بَوَّأْنا لِإِبْراهِيمَ مَكانَ الْبَيْتِ): on the entry of the lām there are three views, because one says «بوّأتُ زيداً منزلاً» (I settled Zayd in a dwelling) [without a lām]. Of the three views, [the first is] that you take it in the sense «جعلنا لإبراهيم مكانَ البيت مُبَوَّأً» (We made the site of the House a place of settlement for Abraham). The second view is that the lām is attached to the maṣdar (verbal noun), like «ومن يرد فيه بإلحاد». The third view is that the lām is redundant (zāʾida); this is the view of al-Farrāʾ. He said: [it is] like (رَدِفَ لَكُمْ) [al-Naml: 72]. (أَنْ لا تُشْرِكْ بِي شَيْئاً): on «أن» there are three views. Al-Kisāʾī said: in meaning it is «بأنْ لا». The second view is that «أن» is in the sense of «أي» (that is), like (وَانْطَلَقَ الْمَلَأُ مِنْهُمْ أَنِ امْشُوا) [Ṣād: 6]. The third view is that «أن» is redundant, for tawkīd (emphasis), like (فَلَمَّا أَنْ جاءَ الْبَشِيرُ) [Yūsuf: 96] «[Translator's note: the printed text gives the reference as Yūsuf: 69; the verse is Yūsuf: 96.]». On His saying (لا تُشْرِكْ بِي شَيْئاً) and (وَأَذِّنْ فِي النَّاسِ بِالْحَجِّ) and the address between them there are three views, all from the scholars. As for the view of the earlier authorities, all of this is an address to Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him, as Ḥammād ibn Salama related from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr from Ibn ʿAbbās: He said to Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him: (أَذِّنْ فِي النَّاسِ بِالْحَجِّ). So he began not to pass by any people without saying: "A House has been built for you, so make pilgrimage to it", and everything — rock, tree and other things — answered him: "Labbayka, Allāhumma, labbayk" (Here I am, O Allah, here I am). Ḥammād ibn Salama related from Abū ʿĀṣim al-Ghanawī from Abū al-Ṭufayl, who said:
Ibn ʿAbbās said: Do you know what the origin of the talbiya was? I said: No. He said: When Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him, was commanded to proclaim the pilgrimage among the people, the mountains lowered their heads for him and the towns were raised up for him, and he called the people to the pilgrimage, and everything answered him: "Labbayka, Allāhumma, labbayk". This is one view. It has also been said: (أَنْ لا تُشْرِكْ بِي شَيْئاً وَطَهِّرْ بَيْتِيَ لِلطَّائِفِينَ) is addressed to Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him, and the speech is complete there. Then Allah, Majestic and Mighty, addressed Muḥammad, peace be upon him, saying: (وَأَذِّنْ فِي النَّاسِ بِالْحَجِّ), that is, inform them that the pilgrimage is incumbent on them. The third view is that all of this is an address to the Prophet ﷺ; this is the view of the people of reasoning (ahl al-naẓar), because the Qurʾān was sent down to the Prophet, peace be upon him, so every address in it is to him unless a decisive proof indicates otherwise. Here there is another proof indicating that the address is to the Prophet, peace be upon him, namely «أنْ لا تُشرك» with the tāʾ, which is an address to someone present, whereas Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him, is absent. On this view the meaning is: "And when We settled for Ibrāhīm the site of the House, We made for you the proofs of the oneness of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, and that Ibrāhīm used to worship Allah alone; so do not associate anything with Me, and purify My House for those who circle it, those who stand, and those who bow and prostrate, and proclaim the pilgrimage among the people." It has been said: the meaning is: inform them that you will perform the Farewell Pilgrimage, so that they perform the pilgrimage. (يَأْتُوكَ رِجالًا): [«رجالاً»] is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). (وَعَلى كُلِّ ضامِرٍ يَأْتِينَ): there are three views on it: «يأتين», because the meaning of «ضامر» is the meaning of «ضوامر» (lean mounts, plural), so He described it with «يأتين»; in some readings «يأتون», which would refer to the people.
Al-Farrāʾ said: «يأتي» is also permissible, following the wording.

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: (ثُمَّ لْيَقْضُوا تَفَثَهُمْ): the people of Kufa read it with the lām given sukūn. This is a far-fetched option in Arabic, because one can pause on «ثمّ», and one may not begin with a vowelless letter; its permissibility, despite its remoteness, is [on the basis] that «ثمّ» is a conjunction like the wāw and the fāʾ. The mīm of «ثمّ» was given fatḥa because of the meeting of two vowelless letters; it may not be given ḍamma or kasra, because it is not inflected. The implied form in Arabic is «ثم ليقضوا أجلَ تفثهم» (then let them complete the term of their ritual cleaning), like (وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ) [Yūsuf: 82]. (وَلْيُوفُوا نُذُورَهُمْ): there are three views on it: the lām with kasra according to the original form; giving it sukūn because of the heaviness of the kasra; and the third is that ʿĀṣim read (وَلْيُوفُوا نُذُورَهُمْ) «[Translator's note: the printed text gives ʿĀṣim's reading in the same form as the standard text; the reading transmitted from ʿĀṣim (via Abū Bakr) is «وَلْيُوَفُّوا», with the fāʾ doubled.]».

nahhas-irab:30-30.t: (ذلِكَ وَمَنْ يُعَظِّمْ حُرُماتِ اللَّهِ), that is, the matter is that, of the obligations; and the meaning is: whoever holds the commission of what is forbidden to be grave, out of reverence for Allah, Majestic and Mighty, and fear of Him. (فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَهُ) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). (إِلَّا ما يُتْلى عَلَيْكُمْ): [«ما»] is in the position of accusative as the excepted (mustathnā). (فَاجْتَنِبُوا الرِّجْسَ مِنَ الْأَوْثانِ): according to the grammarians «مِن» is for clarifying the genus (bayān al-jins), except that al-Akhfash claimed it is partitive, that is: "avoid the filth that is of the idols", that is, worshipping them. This is an unusual but good view.

nahhas-irab:31-31.t: (حُنَفاءَ) is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and likewise (غَيْرَ مُشْرِكِينَ). (وَمَنْ يُشْرِكْ بِاللَّهِ فَكَأَنَّما خَرَّ مِنَ السَّماءِ), that is, on the Day of Resurrection he will have no power to benefit himself nor to ward off punishment from himself, like one who has fallen from the sky and cannot ward off from himself what he is in. (فَتَخْطَفُهُ الطَّيْرُ), that is, they tear him apart with their talons, and he cannot ward them off from himself. On «تخطفه» there are three readings besides this one. Al-Aʿraj read «فَتَخَطَّفُهُ», with fatḥa on the tāʾ and the khāʾ and the ṭāʾ doubled. Abū Rajāʾ read «فَتَخِطِّفُهُ», with fatḥa on the tāʾ, kasra on the khāʾ and the ṭāʾ doubled; this reading is also related from al-Ḥasan. The third is related from al-Ḥasan: «فَتِخِطِّفُهُ», with kasra on the tāʾ and the khāʾ and the ṭāʾ doubled. «[Translator's note: the printed text vowels all of these variants like the standard reading; they are given here as the descriptions specify.]» In al-Aʿraj's reading the original is «فتختطفه»; then the tāʾ was assimilated into the ṭāʾ and the vowel of the tāʾ was thrown onto the khāʾ. Abū Rajāʾ's reading is on the basis that he gave the khāʾ kasra because of the meeting of two vowelless letters; the last reading is the same, except that he gave the tāʾ kasra according to the dialect of those who say «أنت تِضرب». «السحيق» means the far.

nahhas-irab:32-32.t: (ذلِكَ وَمَنْ يُعَظِّمْ شَعائِرَ اللَّهِ فَإِنَّها مِنْ تَقْوَى الْقُلُوبِ) (32): on (ذلِكَ) there are three views: it may be in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), that is, "that is the command of Allah, Majestic and Mighty"; it may be in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ; and it may be in the position of accusative, that is, "follow that, of the command of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, concerning the pilgrimage". (وَمَنْ يُعَظِّمْ شَعائِرَ اللَّهِ): the best that has been said about it is that the meaning is: whoever honours what he has been commanded in the pilgrimage. They were called «شعائر» because Allah, Majestic and Mighty, made them known (أشعر), that is, notified [people] of them; and his honouring of them is that he does not disobey Allah, Majestic and Mighty, in them. (فَإِنَّها مِنْ تَقْوَى الْقُلُوبِ), that is, of a person's fearing his Lord with his heart; and this is figurative (majāz).

nahhas-irab:34-34.t:
(وَلِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ جَعَلْنا مَنْسَكاً) is the reading of the people of Medina, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim; the Kufans except ʿĀṣim read «مَنْسِكاً» with kasra on the sīn. He said: In my copy from Abū Isḥāq: «مَنْسَك» with fatḥa on the sīn is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of «النُّسُك» and «النُّسُوك» (ritual worship), and «مَنْسِك» means a place of ritual worship, like «مَجْلِس». Abū Jaʿfar said: This is an ugly mistake. That holds only for [verbs of the pattern] «فَعَلَ يَفْعِلُ», such as «جَلَسَ يَجْلِسُ», whose maṣdar is «مَجْلَس» and whose place is «مَجْلِس». As for «فَعَلَ يَفْعُلُ», a «مَفْعِل» is not formed from it as a noun of place nor as a maṣdar, unless something is heard [from the Arabs] and is transmitted as heard; although what is frequent in the speech of the Arabs is «مَنْسَك», and that is the analogical form and the [regular] pattern. «منسك» occurs in the speech of the Arabs in three ways: as a maṣdar, as an adverb of time, and as an adverb of place. Al-Farrāʾ said: «المنسك» in the speech of the Arabs is the habitual place [one frequents] for good or evil. It has been said: the «مناسك» of the pilgrimage [are so called] because of people's going back and forth to them. (فَإِلهُكُمْ إِلهٌ واحِدٌ), that is, do not mention over your sacrifices the name of anyone other than Him. (وَبَشِّرِ الْمُخْبِتِينَ): from the people of tafsīr there are three views on it:
ʿAmr ibn Aws said: the «مخبت» is the one who does not wrong [others], and when he is wronged does not seek revenge. Al-Walīd ibn ʿAbd Allāh said: the «مخبتون» are those sincere to Allah, Majestic and Mighty. Mujāhid said: they are those at peace with the command of Allah, Majestic and Mighty. Abū Jaʿfar said: «الخَبْت» of land is the level, low-lying place; its derivation is from this.

nahhas-irab:35-35.t:
(الَّذِينَ إِذا ذُكِرَ اللَّهُ وَجِلَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ) [fearful] lest they disobey Him and be punished. (وَالصَّابِرِينَ عَلى ما أَصابَهُمْ), that is, they endure hardships in obedience and in forbidding wrong. (وَالْمُقِيمِي الصَّلاةِ): there are three views on it:
(وَالْمُقِيمِي الصَّلاةِ) in the genitive through iḍāfa (annexation), with the nūn dropped from it. The accusative with the nūn dropped is also permissible, because the alif and lām are in the sense of «الذي»; this is the view of Sībawayh. Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā [Thaʿlab] said: the accusative with the nūn dropped is permissible, treating it like the singular, because in the singular you make [its object] accusative, saying «هو الآخذُ درهماً» (he is the one taking a dirham). The third view, in ordinary speech, is «والمقيمين الصلاةَ», according to the original form.

nahhas-irab:36-36.t:
(وَالْبُدْنَ جَعَلْناها لَكُمْ): [«البدن»] is accusative through an implied verb like the second [i.e. like «جعلناها»]. Ibn Abī Isḥāq read «والبُدُن» with ḍamma on the bāʾ and the dāl, and the same is related from ʿĪsā, al-Ḥasan and Abū Jaʿfar. Al-Farrāʾ related that one says, for the singular, «بَدَنة» and «بَدَن». Abū Jaʿfar said: so «بُدْن» and «بُدُن» are like «وُثْن» and «وُثُن»; and «بُدُن», it is said, is a plural of a plural, that is, «بدنة», «بِدان», «بُدُن». If someone asks: why has «بَدَنة / بُدْن» become more eloquent, while «خَشَبة / خُشُب» is more eloquent, though the pattern is the same? The answer is that «بَدَنة» is originally an adjective from «البَدانة», which is fatness, whereas «خشبة» «[Translator's note: the printed text has «خشية» here, evidently a misprint for «خشبة».]» is not an adjective; an adjective is more fitting for sukūn, and what is not an adjective is more fitting for a vowel. Do you not see their saying «خَذْلة / خَذْلات», «حُلْوة / حُلْوات», versus «جَفْنة / جَفَنات», «ظُلْمة / ظُلُمات»? (فَاذْكُرُوا اسْمَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْها صَوافَّ): there are three readings of it that have been read:
The reading of the generality is (صَوافَّ). From al-Ḥasan and al-Aʿraj: «صوافي», then it is the plural of «صافية», the pure [one, dedicated to Allah]. From ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: «صوافن», plural of «صافنة». Al-Farrāʾ said: «الصافنة» is the standing one; others related that it is the one standing on three [legs]; Abū ʿUbayda related that «الصافنة» is the one that has drawn its legs together and raised its hoof; and Abū ʿUmar al-Jarmī said: «الصافن» is a vein at the front of the leg; when a horse is struck on it, it raises its legs. (فَإِذا وَجَبَتْ جُنُوبُها): Miqsam said from Ibn ʿAbbās:
"When they fall on their sides."

nahhas-irab:37-37.t: (لَنْ يَنالَ اللَّهَ لُحُومُها) [with «ينال»] according to the masculine of the plural; and it is said [«تنال»] «[Translator's note: the feminine variant is not spelled out in the printed text.]» according to the feminine of the group. (وَلكِنْ يَنالُهُ التَّقْوى), because «التقوى» and «التُّقى» are the same, and «يناله» follows the wording of «التقوى». (وَبَشِّرِ الْمُحْسِنِينَ), that is, those who did well in fulfilling what was incumbent on them.

nahhas-irab:39-39.t:
(أُذِنَ لِلَّذِينَ يُقاتَلُونَ بِأَنَّهُمْ ظُلِمُوا وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلى نَصْرِهِمْ لَقَدِيرٌ) (39): on (أُذِنَ لِلَّذِينَ يُقاتَلُونَ) there are three readings. The one we have given is the reading of the people of Medina. Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim read (أُذِنَ) as the people of Medina read it, and read «يُقاتِلون» with kasra on the tāʾ. The Kufans except ʿĀṣim read «أَذِنَ» with fatḥa on the hamza, and «الذين يقاتِلون» with kasra on the tāʾ. The meanings in this are close to one another, because they both fought and were fought; but the reading of the people of Medina is sounder in meaning and clearer, for two reasons. One of them is that it is soundly established from Ibn ʿAbbās that it was the first verse revealed about fighting. Abū Jaʿfar said: as Abū al-Ḥasan Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Ḥammād al-Ṭihrānī narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us from al-Thawrī from al-Aʿmash from Muslim from Saʿīd from Ibn ʿAbbās that he used to read it (أُذِنَ لِلَّذِينَ يُقاتَلُونَ) and said: it is the first verse revealed about fighting.
Al-Ṭihrānī said: I do not know how the reading is; but if it was the first verse revealed about fighting, then they had not yet fought. So it is unlikely that it be «أُذِن للذين يقاتِلون» [with kasra], and «يقاتَلون» was evident. The other reason is that after it comes «بأنّهم ظُلموا», and after that (الَّذِينَ أُخْرِجُوا); so it must also be «يقاتَلون» [passive]. «بأنّهم ظلموا» and «لأنّهم ظلموا» are one [in meaning], as you say: «جزيتُه ببغيه» and «لبغيه» (I requited him for his transgression). Abū Isḥāq said: «وأنّ الله على نصرهم لقدير» with fatḥa on the hamza is not permissible, because when «إنّ» has the lām with it, giving it fatḥa is not permissible.

nahhas-irab:40-40.t: (الَّذِينَ أُخْرِجُوا مِنْ دِيارِهِمْ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ): [«الذين»] is in the position of genitive as a badal (substitute) for «الذين». (إِلَّا أَنْ يَقُولُوا رَبُّنَا اللَّهُ): [«أن يقولوا»] is in the position of accusative according to the school of Sībawayh, as an exception not of the same kind as the first (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ). Al-Farrāʾ said: «أن» may be in the position of genitive, construing it as referring back to the bāʾ; this is the view of Abū Isḥāq, and the meaning according to him is: "those who were driven out of their homes without right except for saying: Our Lord is Allah", that is, they were driven out for their affirmation of [Allah's] oneness. The idol-worshippers drove them out. (وَلَوْلا دَفْعُ اللَّهِ النَّاسَ بَعْضَهُمْ بِبَعْضٍ): it is related from Abū al-Dardāʾ that he said: Were it not that Allah, Majestic and Mighty, wards off by means of those in the mosques from those who are not in the mosques, and by means of those who go on campaign from those who do not, He would show them the punishment. Ibn Abī Najīḥ related from Mujāhid: were it not that Allah, Majestic and Mighty, wards off through taking rights by testimonies (لَهُدِّمَتْ صَوامِعُ وَبِيَعٌ وَصَلَواتٌ وَمَساجِدُ). «صوامع» and «مساجد» are not inflected (diptote), because they are plurals, and they are the ultimate form of plurals, so they became heavy and were barred from full inflection. Likewise every plural whose third letter is an alif followed by two or three letters. As for His saying, Majestic and Mighty, (يُذْكَرُ فِيهَا اسْمُ اللَّهِ كَثِيراً): what is required in the speech of the Arabs, on careful reflection, is that «يذكر فيها اسم الله» refer back to «المساجد» and not to anything else, because the pronoun is adjacent to it; it may also refer back to «صوامع» and what comes after it, the meaning then being: in the time of their [valid] laws and their upholding of the prescribed penalties and the truth.

nahhas-irab:41-42.t: (الَّذِينَ إِنْ مَكَّنَّاهُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ): Abū Isḥāq said: (الَّذِينَ) is in the position of accusative, referring back to «مَن», meaning in «ولينصرنّ الله من ينصره». Others said: «الذين» is in the position of genitive, referring back to His saying (أُذِنَ لِلَّذِينَ يُقاتَلُونَ); then (الَّذِينَ إِنْ مَكَّنَّاهُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ) would be about four of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, since no others of those of whom it was said (أُذِنَ لِلَّذِينَ يُقاتَلُونَ) were established in the land: they are Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthmān and ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with them. This verse, along with other verses, is used as proof for the imamate of Abū Bakr and ʿUmar. Abū Jaʿfar said: We have already mentioned the full inflection of (وَثَمُودُ) and its absence.

nahhas-irab:45-45.t: (وَبِئْرٍ مُعَطَّلَةٍ): al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: that is, abandoned. Al-Jaḥdarī read (وَبِئْرٍ مُعَطَّلَةٍ) «[Translator's note: the variant has evidently been lost in the printed text, which gives it in the standard form; al-Jaḥdarī's reading is reported elsewhere as «مُعْطَلَةٍ».]», and the meaning is the same. In this is the greatest admonition: Allah, Majestic and Mighty, admonished them by means of peoples who had been destroyed while their traces remained, which they recognized. Al-Aṣmaʿī said: I asked Nāfiʿ ibn Abī Nuʿaym: do you pronounce the hamza in «البئر» and «الذئب»? He said: if the Arabs pronounce the hamza in them, then pronounce it. Most of the transmissions from Nāfiʿ have the hamza in both, except Warsh, whose transmission from him is without hamza in both; the original is with hamza. Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā said: «الذئب» (the wolf) is derived from «تذاءبت الريح» (the wind came from many directions), and so is the wolf. Abū Jaʿfar said: When the hamza is dropped while it is vowelless, after the sukūn the only option is to change it into what matches what precedes it. Al-Farrāʾ holds that «وبئرٍ» is conjoined to «عروضها» «[Translator's note: thus in the printed text; the word in the verse is (عُرُوشِها).]», and Abū Isḥāq holds that it is conjoined [as dependent] on «قرية», that is, "and of a well". Then He said: «أخذتُها وإليّ المصير» «[Translator's note: the printed text has «وإلى المصير»; the verse (al-Ḥajj: 48) reads (أَخَذْتُها وَإِلَيَّ الْمَصِيرُ).]». Abū Isḥāq said: that is, with punishment; then it was omitted because what precedes it indicates it: (وَيَسْتَعْجِلُونَكَ بِالْعَذابِ).

nahhas-irab:52-52.t:
This verse is difficult from two angles. One of them is that some hold that among the prophets — the blessings of Allah be upon them all — there are those who were sent as messengers and those who were not. Others hold that one may not be called a prophet (nabī) unless he is a messenger (mursal). The proof of the soundness of this is His saying, Majestic and Mighty, (وَما أَرْسَلْنا مِنْ قَبْلِكَ مِنْ رَسُولٍ وَلا نَبِيٍّ), so He affirmed the sending for the prophet. The meaning of «نبيّ» is one who conveys news from Allah, Majestic and Mighty, and the meaning of conveying news from Allah, Majestic and Mighty, is the sending itself.
The other angle in which the difficulty lies is the ḥadīth that is related. Abū Jaʿfar said: We have mentioned it with its isnād; it is that the Prophet ﷺ recited: «أفرأيتم اللات والعزّى فإنّ شفاعتهم ترتجى» (Have you considered al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā? for their intercession is hoped for), «وسها» (and he made a slip) — thus in the transmission of al-Zuhrī; and in the transmission of others: «فإنّهنّ الغرانيق العلى» (for they are the exalted cranes). Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning of this must be ascertained from the standpoint of religion, because of the attacks made on it by those of the heretics who attack it. The first point is that the ḥadīth does not have a connected isnād; and even if its isnād were connected and sound, its meaning would be sound. As for the meaning of «وسها», its meaning is "and he dropped". Its implied form would then be: (أَفَرَأَيْتُمُ اللَّاتَ وَالْعُزَّى), and the speech is complete; then he dropped «والغرانيق العلى», meaning the angels, «فإنّ شفاعتهم», the pronoun referring back to the angels. As for whoever relates «فإنّهنّ الغرانيق العلى», for his transmission there are answers: one is that a verb of saying is omitted, as the Arabs use in many things; it may also be without omission, as a rebuke, because before it is «أفرأيتم», so it would be an argument against them. If it was in the prayer, speaking was [at that time] permitted in the prayer. It may also be that the pronoun is for the angels, just as something whose meaning is known is referred to by a pronoun; then Allah, Majestic and Mighty, abrogated that because of the benefit in it. The benefit in it is the removal of deception, lest some people be deceived and told: this pronoun is for al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā. So Allah, Majestic and Mighty, sent down (وَما أَرْسَلْنا مِنْ قَبْلِكَ مِنْ رَسُولٍ وَلا نَبِيٍّ إِلَّا إِذا تَمَنَّى أَلْقَى الشَّيْطانُ فِي أُمْنِيَّتِهِ فَيَنْسَخُ اللَّهُ ما يُلْقِي الشَّيْطانُ).
There are two other views on the verse. One of them is that the meaning is: when he recited (أَفَرَأَيْتُمُ اللَّاتَ وَالْعُزَّى), a man on whose tongue Satan cast it said: «فإنّهنّ الغرانيق العلى». The other view is that ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning the saying of Allah, Majestic and Mighty:
(إِلَّا إِذا تَمَنَّى): he said: when he spoke, Satan cast corruption into his «أمنيّة»; he said: [that is,] into his speech; (فَيَنْسَخُ اللَّهُ ما يُلْقِي الشَّيْطانُ): he said: so Allah nullifies what Satan casts. This is among the best, highest and most excellent of what has been said about the verse. Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Ḥanbal said: In Egypt there is a scroll of tafsīr related by ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa; if a man travelled to Egypt for its sake alone, it would not be too much.
The meaning according to it is that when the Prophet ﷺ spoke to himself, Satan cast into his speech by way of a stratagem, saying to him: "If only you asked Allah, Majestic and Mighty, to give you such-and-such as booty, so that the Muslims would have more means"; while Allah, Majestic and Mighty, knows that the benefit lies in something else, so He nullifies what Satan casts — as Ibn ʿAbbās said. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ both related «تمنّى» in the sense "he spoke to himself"; this is what is well known in the language. They also both related «تمنّى» in the sense "he recited", and that is related from al-Ḍaḥḥāk.

nahhas-irab:55-55.t: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī related «في مُرْيَةٍ» with ḍamma on the mīm, but the kasra is better known. (حَتَّى تَأْتِيَهُمُ السَّاعَةُ بَغْتَةً): Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: [«بغتة»] is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). (أَوْ يَأْتِيَهُمْ عَذابُ يَوْمٍ عَقِيمٍ): the Day of Resurrection is called «عقيم» (barren) because no day like it follows after it.

nahhas-irab:63-63.t:
«فتصبحُ» is not an apodosis (jawāb); according to al-Khalīl, may Allah have mercy on him, it is only a statement (khabar). Al-Khalīl said: the meaning is "Take heed: He sent down water from the sky, and such-and-such happened", as [the poet] said: [al-Ṭawīl] 304-
ألم تسأل الرّبع القوّاء فينطق ... وهل تخيرنك اليوم بيداء سملق
(Did you not ask the desolate encampment, and it speaks? And will a barren desert tell you anything today?)
Al-Farrāʾ said: «ألم تر» is a statement, as you say in ordinary speech: "Know that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sends down water from the sky, and the earth becomes green."

nahhas-irab:65-65.t: (وَالْفُلْكَ تَجْرِي فِي الْبَحْرِ بِأَمْرِهِ): [that is,] "and He subjected the ships"; the meaning may also be «وأنّ الفلك»; and the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) is also permissible. (وَيُمْسِكُ السَّماءَ أَنْ تَقَعَ): [«أن تقع»] is in the position of accusative, that is, "He holds back the sky, out of aversion to its falling on the earth".

nahhas-irab:72-72.t: (قُلْ أَفَأُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِشَرٍّ مِنْ ذلِكُمُ النَّارُ): on [«النار»] there are three views: the nominative, in the sense «هو النار» or «هي النار» (it is the Fire); the genitive as a badal (substitute); and the accusative, in which there are three views: it may be in the sense «أعني» (I mean); by an implied verb like the second; or construed according to the meaning, that is, «أُعَرِّفُكم بشرٍّ من ذلكم النارَ» (I make known to you something worse than that: the Fire).

nahhas-irab:73-73.t: (يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ ضُرِبَ مَثَلٌ): the best that has been said about it is that the meaning is: a parable has been struck for Allah, Majestic and Mighty, of what is worshipped besides Him.

nahhas-irab:78-78.t:
(وَجاهِدُوا فِي اللَّهِ حَقَّ جِهادِهِ): Abū Isḥāq said: it has been said that this is abrogated. He said: and likewise (اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ تُقاتِهِ) [Āl ʿImrān: 102]. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is something in which abrogation cannot occur, because it is obligatory on a person, as Ḥaywa ibn Shurayḥ related from Abū Hāniʾ al-Khawlānī from ʿAmr ibn Mālik from Faḍāla ibn ʿUbayd from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The mujāhid is the one who strives against his own soul for the sake of Allah, Majestic and Mighty"; and as Abū Ṭālib related from Abū Usāma that a man asked the Prophet ﷺ at the first Jamra: which jihad is best? He did not answer him. Then he asked him at the second Jamra, and he did not answer him. Then he asked him at Jamrat al-ʿAqaba, and he, peace be upon him, said: "Where is the questioner?" He said: "Here I am." He ﷺ said: "A word of justice before a tyrannical ruler." (هُوَ اجْتَباكُمْ): by this He indicated the excellence of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and a refutation of whoever disparages them, because He, Majestic and Mighty, chose them to support His Prophet, peace be upon him. (وَما جَعَلَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِي الدِّينِ مِنْ حَرَجٍ): [«حرج»] is in the position of accusative, and «مِن» is redundant (zāʾida), for tawkīd (emphasis). (مِلَّةَ أَبِيكُمْ إِبْراهِيمَ): al-Farrāʾ said: that is, «كملّة أبيكم» (like the religion of your father); when you drop the kāf you make it accusative, that is, "He has made it easy for you, like the religion of your father". He said:
and if you wish you may make it accusative as a command. Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning is «اتّبعوا ملّة أبيكم» (follow the religion of your father). He said: (هُوَ سَمَّاكُمُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ) may refer to Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him, that is, he named you Muslims in what came before; (وَفِي هذا), that is, and in his judgement that whoever follows Muḥammad ﷺ is a monotheist, he has named you Muslims. Abū Jaʿfar said: This view contradicts the view of the leading scholars. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās: «هو سمّاكم المسلمين»: he said: [it is] Allah, Majestic and Mighty; and likewise Ibn Jurayj related from ʿAṭāʾ from Ibn ʿAbbās. Ibn [Abī] Najīḥ «[Translator's note: the printed text has «ابن نجيح»; elsewhere this transmitter is «ابن أبي نجيح».]» related from Mujāhid concerning His saying, Majestic and Mighty, (هُوَ سَمَّاكُمُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ مِنْ قَبْلُ): he said: He named you Muslims before, in the Books and the Reminder, and in this Qurʾān. (لِيَكُونَ الرَّسُولُ شَهِيداً عَلَيْكُمْ), that is, through his conveying [the message] to you
and your responding to him; (وَتَكُونُوا شُهَداءَ عَلَى النَّاسِ) through your conveying it to them and what you see of them. (وَاعْتَصِمُوا بِاللَّهِ): it has been said: that is, hold yourselves back from sins by means of the strength and freedom of action He has given you.
(هُوَ مَوْلاكُمْ), that is, the Master of your blessings and the Master of what you need in your lives. For this reason, from this angle, it was disliked that a person be addressed "O my master (مولاي)", and that one say: "This is my slave (عبدي)" or "my slave-girl (أمتي)". The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Rather let him say: my lad (فتاي), or my lass (فتاتي)." (فَنِعْمَ الْمَوْلى), that is, how excellent a Protector for you, because He wills good for you; (وَنِعْمَ النَّصِيرُ) for whoever obeys Him.
